era: GameCube / PlayStation 2 / Xbox / PSP / PlayStation 3 / Xbox 360 / Wii
summary: Def Jam-branded fighting and music games; use GameCube for Vendetta, Xbox for Fight for NY, PSP/PPSSPP for The Takeover, and HD-console routes for Icon and Rapstar.

entries.title: Def Jam Vendetta
entries.definitive_edition: GameCube primary plus Japanese release for exclusive characters

emulation.notes: Use Dolphin for the primary GameCube route; use PCSX2 or Dolphin for the Japanese exclusive roster check.

primary.why: Vendetta shipped on PlayStation 2 and GameCube; GameCube is selected as the main local-preservation route, while the Japanese releases are secondary because they include Japan-exclusive rappers Dabo and S-Word.
primary.how_to_play: Play the GameCube version on original hardware or Dolphin with internal-resolution scaling; sample the Japanese release only for the exclusive roster additions.

secondary.exclusive_content: Japanese rappers Dabo and S-Word appear exclusively in the Japanese release.
secondary.what_to_play: Sample versus/exhibition play with Dabo and S-Word.
secondary.why: Exclusive roster content is absent from the primary English-language GameCube route.

all_releases.reason: skip: same core game as GameCube without being the selected primary route.
primary: selected local-preservation route for the main English-language game.

all_releases.fidelity: Japanese regional release with exclusive Dabo and S-Word roster appearances.
all_releases.reason: secondary: play only for the Japan-exclusive characters.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: The English GameCube route is the practical main playthrough; the Japanese regional release has exclusive roster content to sample separately.

entries.title: Def Jam: Fight for NY

emulation.notes: Use Xbox hardware/Xemu if compatibility is good; PS2 is the fallback full-feature console route.

primary.why: Fight for NY shipped on GameCube, PlayStation 2, Xbox, and later PSP; the GameCube version is documented as missing voices, music tracks, blur effects, and some crowd density, while Xbox and PS2 keep the fuller console feature set. Xbox is selected as the highest-fidelity sixth-generation console route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox version on original hardware or Xemu if compatible; use the PSP Takeover entry separately if you want that handheld version.

all_releases.fidelity: GameCube release with documented missing voices, eight music tracks, blur effects, and reduced crowds in some arenas.
all_releases.reason: skip: content/presentation reductions make it a non-primary route.
skip: full-featured route, but Xbox is selected as the higher-fidelity console target.
primary: full feature set without the GameCube omissions and the strongest console preservation target.

all_releases.fidelity: Handheld port released as Def Jam Fight for NY: The Takeover.
all_releases.reason: skip: treated as its own entry because it is a distinct PSP version.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: GameCube is lower-completeness due documented omissions; Xbox is the main console route, while PSP is handled separately.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster or rerelease exists; licensing has kept original discs in demand.

entries.title: Def Jam Fight for NY: The Takeover

emulation.notes: Use PPSSPP for cleaner handheld output.

primary.why: The Takeover is the PSP version of Fight for NY and is documented as the handheld port of the second Def Jam fighting game.
primary.how_to_play: Play on PSP hardware or PPSSPP with internal-resolution scaling.

all_releases.reason: primary: only sourced platform route for The Takeover.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Handheld version should not replace the full console Fight for NY route; treat it as a separate PSP entry.

emulation.notes: Use original hardware where compatibility is uncertain.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Native HD-console output or Xbox 360 emulation

primary.why: Icon released on PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 as the HD-era Def Jam fighter with changeable soundtrack mechanics; Xbox 360 is selected as the primary preservation target while PS3 remains an equivalent alternate route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Xbox 360 hardware or a compatible preservation setup; use the PS3 release if that is the available original hardware route.

all_releases.reason: skip: same core game as Xbox 360, selected as alternate rather than primary.
primary: selected HD preservation target for the same-platform content set.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: No sourced exclusive content difference between the two HD-console versions is asserted here.

emulation.emulator: Original PS3 hardware / RPCS3 if compatible
emulation.notes: Microphone/camera support is the preservation constraint.

primary.why: Rapstar released on PlayStation 3, Wii, and Xbox 360 as a rap-karaoke game; PlayStation 3 is selected as the HD primary route, with Xbox 360 as a comparable HD alternate and Wii as the lower-fidelity route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS3 version with compatible microphones/camera hardware; use Xbox 360 if that is the available HD setup.

all_releases.fidelity: HD-console release with microphone/camera performance setup.

all_releases.reason: skip: lower-fidelity route than the HD console versions.
skip: comparable HD alternate, but PS3 is selected to keep one primary row.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Peripheral and online-feature availability may affect preservation more than raw platform fidelity.
